title: OCCURS DEPENDING ON — variable-length table tied to a separate count field
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. POLICY-LOAD.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-POLICY.
           05  WS-RIDER-COUNT      PIC 9(2).
           05  WS-RIDERS           OCCURS 1 TO 50 TIMES
                                   DEPENDING ON WS-RIDER-COUNT
                                   INDEXED BY WS-IX.
               10  WS-RIDER-CODE   PIC X(4).
               10  WS-RIDER-PREM   PIC 9(5)V99.
      *> The record's *physical* length depends on WS-RIDER-COUNT at
      *> the moment of file-WRITE. Reading the record back without
      *> first restoring WS-RIDER-COUNT means OCCURS evaluates to a
      *> stale length -- in the worst case OS-level memory corruption.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       LOAD-RIDERS.
           PERFORM VARYING WS-IX FROM 1 BY 1
              UNTIL WS-IX > WS-RIDER-COUNT
              DISPLAY WS-RIDERS(WS-IX)
           END-PERFORM.
notes:
OCCURS DEPENDING ON is the COBOL idiom for variable-length lists
inside fixed-position records. Migrating to a modern collection
type (List<T> / ArrayList) loses the *physical-length* contract
that callers writing/reading the record rely on, and is a frequent
source of 'works on synthetic data, corrupts on real data' bugs.
The spec must capture the count-field dependency AND surface the
fixed-vs-variable allocation question for the SME.
